subject: QMon onboarding sprint plan & canary/rollback procedures
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QMon kickoff for Acme Health — checklist attached

Hi team,

Looping you in on the QMon (quality monitoring) kickoff for Acme Health. They signed the Dedicated contract and are targeting a phased rollout: embeddings -> chat assistant -> reranking. Key asks from the AMs:

- Prompt sets for each product surface (we'll need hi/lo severity tests)
- Integration points for eval harness + CI gating
- Canary criteria and rollback window (they want short rollbacks for high-risk paths)

I've attached a starter checklist (qmon_onboarding_checklist.xlsx) and a draft canary playbook. Please review and add implementation risks next to each line item.

Proposed kickoff: Wed May 5, 10:00am PT with Acme's engineering + security.

Attachments: qmon_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (xlsx), canary_playbook.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,

Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@acmehealth.com>, Tom Walker <tom.walker@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QMon kickoff for Acme Health — proposed sprint plan and canary/rollback draft

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few follow-ups from my side before the Wed kickoff so we have concrete engineering actions:

1) Sprint plan (3 sprints, two-week cadence)
   - Sprint 1: prompt-set collection + baseline evals (embedding similarity, chat QA set)
   - Sprint 2: eval harness integration, automated CI checks for prompt regressions
   - Sprint 3: canary rollout + runbook rehearsal, monitoring thresholds tuning

2) Eval harness integration: attaching a reference spec (eval-harness-integration.yaml). Dylan, can you confirm the runner (self-hosted vs Redwood-managed) and whether Acme will provide CI tokens?

3) Canary & rollback — draft proposal (we should finalize during kickoff):
   - Canary window: 30 minutes of traffic with mirrored percentage 5-10%
   - Success criteria: error rate < 1% and semantic regression score delta <= 0.12 vs baseline for two consecutive 15-min windows
   - Rollback triggers: error rate spike > 2% OR latency p95 increase > 50ms OR semantic drift > 0.15
   - Rollback action: immediate traffic shift back to previous model + incident page to on-call SRE and CS lead

Elena/Tom: can you confirm whether Acme requires a >1 hour rollback window (for audit) or if they prefer immediate rollbacks with post-mortem? We'll capture as policy either way.

I uploaded the draft playbook and the eval spec to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqExample

Attachments: eval-harness-integration.yaml (yaml)

Thanks — I'll run the kickoff and make sure we leave with an agreed canary threshold and an implementation owner for each sprint item.

Rachel Kim
Principal Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QMon kickoff for Acme Health — proposed sprint plan and canary/rollback draft

Rachel, thanks for the clarity. A few notes from Acme engineering/security: 

- We prefer Redwood-managed eval runs for sprint 2 (we can provide a service account with scoped access).
- Rollback policy: for clinical-facing surfaces we require a formal 1-hour observation window post-launch before declaring success; however we expect rollbacks to be automated if urgent triggers fire (we want immediate mitigation + a 1-hour stewardship period).
- Canary: 5% mirrored traffic for 45 minutes is our conservative starting point.

We also want the prompt set to include 12 safety edge cases and 30 QA prompts across priority intents — I'll attach a minimal prompt list in the follow-up.

On scheduling: Wed May 5 at 10:00am PT works for our engineering and security. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Elena Park
Engineering Manager, Integrations
Acme Health

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Action items & final canary/rollback policy (post-kickoff)

Thanks everyone for a productive kickoff. Summarizing decisions and owners so we can close the loop: 

Decisions:
- Sprint cadence confirmed: three sprints, two weeks each.
- Eval harness: Redwood-managed runner (Dylan to onboard Acme service account by 5/12).
- Canary window: 45 minutes at 5% mirrored traffic for clinical-facing surfaces (per Acme request).
- Rollback policy: immediate automated rollback on urgent triggers (error rate > 2% OR latency p95 +50ms OR semantic drift > 0.15). Post-rollback, a 1-hour stewardship and a joint post-mortem within 48 hours.

Owners & next steps:
- Marissa: finalize prompt sets and surface-specific QA lists by 5/14 (includes 12 safety edge cases).
- Dylan: configure eval harness runner and CI gate; confirm token exchange flow by 5/12. Attachment: eval-harness-integration.yaml
- Monica: production monitoring dashboard templates and alert routing to on-call SRE by 5/18.
- Mina: upload final canary playbook and incident checklist to the shared drive (link below) by 5/13.

Attachments: canary_playbook.pdf, qmon_onboarding_checklist.xlsx, eval-harness-integration.yaml
Shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqExample
HubSpot record: https://redwoodai.app/hubspot/ACME-12345

If no objections, I'll mark this thread as the single source of truth for QMon rollout requirements and move the tickets into the implementation epic. Let me know if any owner needs additional support or if Acme changes the rollback window.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Principal Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
